 Transport associations expect significant delays over the extended national holiday weekend.
 Advertising 
 The Austrian Automobile, Motorcycle and Amateur Sports Association (ARBÖ) predicts heavy delays on the main traffic routes of the country for the extended weekend around the Austrian National Day on October 26, 2026.
 In addition to the convergence of return travel and holiday traffic – due to the start of the autumn holidays in Austria and Baden-Württemberg as well as the end of the holidays in seven other German federal states – high-profile major events in Vienna and Tyrol are causing regional capacity limits in the road network.
 Heavy traffic is expected on the motorway routes from Saturday morning onwards, heading south and towards the Alpine recreation areas. The primary bottlenecks include the Tauern Autobahn (A10) and the West Autobahn (A1) in the greater Salzburg area, the Pyhrn Autobahn (A9) before the toll plazas, and the Inntal Autobahn (A12) near Kufstein and the Ötztal interchange. The Brenner Autobahn (A13) is particularly prone to congestion, where ongoing infrastructure work and the renovation of the Lueg Bridge are reducing capacity. In the greater Vienna area, traffic disruptions are traditionally concentrated on the Südosttangente (A23).
 In the federal capital, Vienna, several major events are leading to temporary road closures and parking capacity overloads. The Austrian Armed Forces' information and performance showcase at Heldenplatz and the "Vienna Security Festival" at Rathausplatz are expected to draw hundreds of thousands of visitors, resulting in the closure of the Vienna Ring Road and delays on the Zweierlinie (a major ring road). Simultaneously, the ATP tennis tournament "Erste Bank Open" at the Wiener Stadthalle and the Marx Halle requires increased attention on the Neubaugürtel. Meanwhile, in Tyrol, the opening of the Alpine Ski World Cup on the Rettenbach Glacier in Sölden is causing capacity bottlenecks on the Ötztalstraße (B186).
 Traffic and mobility organizations advise motorists to allow plenty of extra time and to use public transport when traveling to major urban and sporting events. Depending on weather conditions, the peak traffic rush for day trips and holiday return journeys on the national holiday is expected to continue until late in the evening.
